summary: A way of splitting up the people, places or things your work is about, so you can compare the parts: by region, by depot, by product line.
example: Region: members are split by the growing region they farm in, so regions can be compared.
definition: A way to split what your organisation serves so you can compare the parts. First add the split itself, such as Region, then each part under it, such as Northern region. Gaps, projects, programmes, operations and KPIs use the same segments, so they compare the same parts. A segment says where or what, never who: it is not a role or partner (a resource), not the people the work helps (a beneficiary group), not a team, not a free tag, and not a period of time.

/spec/parent.guide: The split this is one part of, such as Region for Northern region, or a larger part it sits inside. Leave it empty for the split itself.

poor.why: A team, not a segment. Choose the split this part belongs to, here Depot.

/spec/description.guide: What is in this part and what is not, including borderline cases.
good: Which collection depot produce passed through. Every depot in the network is a value; produce collected in the field is counted against the depot it was taken to.
Which line produce belongs to. A crate is counted against one line only, by what it mostly holds.

poor.why: Does not say where a region's boundary comes from, so two people could count a holding differently.
Says why it matters, not what falls inside it.

/metadata/name.guide: The name of the split, such as Region, or of one part, such as Northern region.

poor.why: A role, so it is a resource. Use the depot itself as the segment.
The people the work is for, which is a beneficiary group. Slice by where they work (Depot) if you need to compare.
Who carries the work, which is a team.
A period of time. Use a reporting cycle.
A free label, not a planned way of slicing what you serve.

Gap:/spec/segments.ask: Which gaps were found in this part?
Gap:/spec/segments.ifNone: None yet is fine. A gap names this segment when its evidence covers it.

KPI:/spec/disaggregations.ask: Which KPIs are split by this?
KPI:/spec/disaggregations.ifNone: None yet is fine. Only a top-level split, such as Region, can break down a KPI, and only when its data source reports by it.
